risks: A broad import from any dirty source can overwrite newer SMP scheduler, ResidentRoot, PageBacked, L4/L6, ext4 lifecycle, or tooling behavior.
A multi-page projection without one retained owner bundle can release a DMA-visible frame or clean a redirtied generation.
Holding RangeLock, Guard, or borrowed PTE state across Yield can deadlock or observe a migrated hart with stale exclusion.
Restoring writable PTEs before I/O and checkpoint terminal settlement can race mmap writers with persisted data and metadata.
Host tests and SMP smoke do not replace Linux image exchange, e2fsck, xfstests, and crash evidence.
